newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Independence Day movie fuels News Corp profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Independence Day movie fuels News Corp profit rise.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. Thursday reported a 10 percent rise in net profit for the first half of 1996/97, led by the movie Independence Day which helped boost Fox films' profits a staggering 154 percent in the period.

News Corp. reported a profit before one-time items of A$731 million ($555 million) for the six months to December 31, compared with A$663 million ($504 million) for the corresponding period a year earlier.
But this was at the lower end of Australian analysts' expectations which ranged between A$735 million ($559 million) and A$775 million ($589 million).

Analysts had said News Corp.'s profits for the first half of this year must be around 15 percent to 20 percent better if Murdoch's group is to achieve its August 1996 forecast of a 20 percent profit rise in the full year to June 30, 1997 from the A$1.26 billion ($985 million) achieved in 1995/96.

"U.S. results were led by Fox Filmed Entertainment which posted a 154 percent gain in operating profits year on year reflecting the continued success of Independence Day," News Corp. said in a statement.

"Since its release in July 1996, ("Independence Day") ID4 has generated more than US$787 million in box office receipts worldwide. Twenty two million copies of the ID4 video have been shipped since its domestic release in November of last year."
News Corp. also cited the recent re-release of George Lucas' classic science fiction movie Star Wars as contributing $36 million in ticket sales in its first weekend's showing.
News Corp. said the majority of its Fox television stations had posted gains in revenue and operating profits.

Fox television's acquisition of the New World Communications Group in January has expanded it to 22 stations and now makes it the United States' largest owned-and-operated television station group, with a combined reach of 40 percent.
Roughly 70 percent of News Corp.'s operating income is generated in U.S. dollars.
In Britain, Murdoch's newspapers, The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times, continued to experience strong growth, posting an 18 percent rise in operating profits year on year.

"All of the company's newspapers have maintained their dominant position in each of their respective markets, despite cover price increases instituted during the quarter at both The Sun and The Times," News Corp. said.
In Australia, Murdoch's newspapers posted slight increases in the quarter, with advertising volumes below last year reflecting a slow economy, the company said.
In Asia, STAR TV continued to lose money, as expected.
